target_customer: Home buyers who need a mortgage, and the agents and sellers who prefer cash offers
problem: Buyers who need a mortgage lose bids to all cash offers because sellers fear financing risk and slow closings.
business_model: Mortgage lender that buys the home with its own cash then sells it to the buyer at the same price, earning mortgage and fee revenue
product_category: Fintech mortgage and cash offer service

competitors.name: Opendoor
competitors.what: iBuyer that buys homes directly from sellers

competitors.name: Zillow Offers
competitors.what: iBuying arm of Zillow competing with Redfin and Opendoor

technical_complexity.rationale: Mostly lending operations, credit checks with national lenders and a warehouse credit facility; software itself is standard.

defensibility.rationale: Mortgage licensing and a credit facility are barriers, but the idea could be copied by lenders and iBuyers.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: HomeLight acquired the company in June 2022 in an all stock deal; Zillow shut its iBuyer arm in November 2021.

market_need_then: Cash offers beat mortgage contingent offers in competitive markets, and the company launched in Colorado in June 2019 after raising 7M USD, reflecting seller preference for certainty.

branding.domain_note: Moved to the accept.inc domain after the October 2020 rename.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain consumer pitch: Buy Now, Mortgage Later.

branding.brand_signature: Buy Now, Mortgage Later tagline (per the YC page).
branding.community_and_virality: Local and trade press covered the launch (Denver7, HousingWire, RealTrends); no fan or merch evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: Trade press coverage helped awareness, but the reason for the rename is not sourced and the final name is a generic word with a domain suffix.

outcome_analysis: BoardRE launched in Colorado in 2019 after a 7M USD first round, renamed itself Accept.inc in October 2020, and raised about 90M USD of debt and equity in June 2021 as housing boomed. HomeLight bought it in June 2022 in an undisclosed all stock deal as real estate tech cooled, with most staff moving to HomeLight, so it was an acquisition rather than a collapse.
notes: The 90M USD June 2021 figure is debt plus equity with no split found, and is recorded as other. Investor list for the 2019 round combines the press release context and a DN Capital post; 1517 Fund was named as prior support. Rename date comes from a CB Insights style summary (early October 2020) and no announcement was found. Site www.accept.inc did not resolve in this environment. Competitors come from a September 2019 article; other 2019 era iBuyers were not in dated sources. Craft.co lists the company as closed, which conflicts with the acquisition sources and is disregarded.
